topic: Medusa & EAGLE: Multi-Head Speculative Decoding Without a Separate Draft Model
title: Medusa and EAGLE: Multi-Head Speculative Decoding Without Draft Models
lead: Traditional speculative decoding requires hosting and synchronizing a secondary draft model in GPU VRAM. Medusa and EAGLE replace the draft model with lightweight prediction heads attached to the base model's final hidden states, generating candidate trees verified in a single forward pass.

stats.title: Inference Acceleration Benchmarks:
items: Medusa achieves 2.2x to 2.8x wall-clock latency speedup on 70B models without dedicating VRAM to a second draft model.
Tree attention masks verify up to 64 speculative candidates in a single tensor core forward pass.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: The Chess Grandmaster Calculating Move Trees
mentalModel.text:
A novice player calculates one move, makes it, and waits for the opponent to react. A grandmaster calculates a branch tree three plies ahead before touching a piece.

Medusa drafts branches of future tokens in parallel: The base model's final hidden state feeds multiple heads simultaneously predicting token t+1, t+2, and t+3. The verification step tests the tree all at once.

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: Draft model speculative decoding incurs high engineering friction due to model pairing and KV synchronization.
Medusa heads add less than 1% to overall model parameter count while doubling decoding throughput.
Tree attention parallelizes candidate verification into standard scaled dot-product attention kernels.
takeaway.badge: Speculative prediction heads eliminate the memory and operational overhead of dual-model serving.

topic: Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) & YaRN: Context Extension Beyond Pre-Training Limits
audience: Frontier AI Researchers & Foundation Model Architects
title: Rotary Embeddings and YaRN: Extending Context Windows from 4k to 128k Tokens
lead: Absolute positional encodings fail to generalize past their pre-training length. Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) rotate query and key vectors in complex 2D planes, while Yet another RoPE extensioN (YaRN) interpolates high-frequency dimensions to extend context windows 16x with minimal fine-tuning.

stats.title: Context Window Scaling & Perplexity Metrics:
items: Naive RoPE context extrapolation causes perplexity to explode past 1.2x training length.
YaRN interpolation extends context from 4k to 128k tokens in fewer than 400 fine-tuning steps while maintaining zero perplexity degradation on short contexts.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: Two Hands on an Analog Clock Face
mentalModel.text:
Absolute positional encoding is like stamping a fixed calendar date onto a page. Relative distance cannot be computed without consulting an index.

RoPE is like an analog clock: The angle between the minute hand and the hour hand directly reflects their relative time delta, regardless of what hour the clock started ticking.

diagram:
graph LR
    Tokens["Query/Key Vectors"] --> Split["Pairwise 2D Feature Channels"]
    Split --> Matrix["Complex Rotation Matrix R(m*theta)"]
    Matrix --> YaRN{"Dimension Band?"}
    YaRN -- "High Frequency (Local)" --> Extrapolate["Extrapolate (No Interpolation)"]
    YaRN -- "Low Frequency (Global)" --> Interpolate["Interpolate by Scale Factor s"]
    Extrapolate --> Rotated["Rotated Attention Vectors (q_rot, k_rot)"]
    Interpolate --> Rotated
    Rotated --> DotProduct["Inner Product: q_rot^T * k_rot = f(q, k, m-n)"]
    style Matrix fill:#1e3a8a,stroke:#60a5fa,color:#fff
    style DotProduct fill:#065f46,stroke:#10b981,color:#fff
diagramCaption: Figure: 2D Complex Vector Rotation and Frequency-Band Interpolation in YaRN
codeContent:
import torch

def compute_yarn_frequencies(dim: int, scale: float = 16.0, base: float = 10000.0):
    pos = torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float()
    inv_freq = 1.0 / (base ** (pos / dim))
    # YaRN frequency modulation
    wavelength = 2 * torch.pi / inv_freq
    # Dimensions with long wavelengths are interpolated; short are extrapolated
    low_freq_wavelen = 4096 * 0.1
    high_freq_wavelen = 4096 * 1.0
    
    yarn_freq = torch.where(
        wavelength > high_freq_wavelen, 
        inv_freq / scale, 
        inv_freq
    )
    return yarn_freq

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: RoPE naturally expresses relative distance through the inner product of rotated vectors.
Linear position interpolation blurs high-frequency local tokens, damaging syntax parsing.
Targeted frequency-band scaling (YaRN) preserves sharp local attention while extending long-range document recall.
takeaway.badge: Harmonic frequency interpolation turns rigid context boundaries into elastic context windows.

topic: Triton GPU Kernels for LLMs: Writing Fused Attention and RMSNorm Without CUDA C++
title: Triton GPU Programming: Fusing Memory-Bound Kernels for 3x Faster Inference
lead: Standard PyTorch operations write intermediate tensors to GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) between every layer. By writing custom block-level kernels in OpenAI Triton, systems engineers fuse RMSNorm and Softmax directly inside on-chip SRAM, cutting memory bandwidth bottlenecks by over 60%.

stats.title: Memory Bandwidth & Latency Benchmarks:
items: Unfused LayerNorm + GeLU executes 3 discrete round-trips to GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM).
A fused Triton RMSNorm kernel keeps activations in on-chip SRAM registers, delivering 3.4x higher arithmetic throughput on NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: In-Memory Cooking vs. Trips to the Walk-in Freezer
mentalModel.text:
Unfused GPU operations are like a chef who chops an onion, walks to the warehouse freezer to store it, immediately walks back to retrieve it, and sautees it.

Kernel fusion keeps the ingredients on the cutting board (SRAM): Operations are chained sequentially within high-speed registers before writing the final cooked dish back to global memory.

diagram:
graph TD
 In["Input Tensor in Global HBM (Slow, High Capacity)"] --> Load["Triton Block Load to On-Chip SRAM (3.3 TB/s)"]
 Load --> Mean["Compute Variance in Parallel Registers"]
 Mean --> Rsqrt["Multiply by Fast rsqrt"]
 Rsqrt --> Scale["Multiply by Learnable Weight Gamma"]
 Scale --> Store["Single Fused Write Back to HBM"]
 style Load fill:#1e3a8a,stroke:#60a5fa,color:#fff
 style Store fill:#065f46,stroke:#10b981,color:#fff
diagramCaption: Figure: Fused Kernel Execution Workflow in High-Speed On-Chip SRAM
codeContent:
# Conceptual Triton RMSNorm Kernel
# Kernel keeps intermediate activation statistics in high-speed SRAM registers
def rmsnorm_fused_step(x, weight, eps=1e-6):
 variance = x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
 return x * torch.rsqrt(variance + eps) * weight

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: Modern LLM generation is memory-bandwidth bound, not compute FLOP bound.
Triton abstracts CUDA thread hierarchies into block-level array programming.
Fusing elementwise and normalization operations eliminates intermediate memory writes entirely.
takeaway.badge: On-chip kernel fusion unlocks hardware potential without writing thousands of lines of CUDA C++.
